    Chapter I — Background

    Engineering judgment
    into intelligence

    Edwin Isac · Dublin, Ireland · MSc Data & Computational Science (UCD)

    I build AI systems that understand where automation ends and human judgment begins. 4+ years in production ML — NLP, computer vision, real-time data systems. Currently focused on LLM-powered multi-agent systems where humans and agents collaborate.

    My work lives at the intersection of philosophy and engineering: cryptographic audit trails for AI accountability, evaluation frameworks that measure truthfulness, and tools that make complex systems transparent to the people who depend on them.

    IV
    Chapter IV — Philosophy
    The best AI systems aren't autonomous — they're collaborative.

    I design for the human in the loop because judgment, context, and accountability can't be fully automated. My work asks: where should the machine stop and the human begin? That boundary is where value lives.

    Philosophy isn't decoration — it's engineering. Understanding epistemology helps me build better evaluation frameworks. Understanding ethics helps me design audit trails that actually matter. Every system I build carries a thesis about how humans and machines should relate.
